title: CHOOSE study
official: Use of the Checkpoint inhibitor DOstarlimab in the endOmetrial cancer fertility-Sparing trEatment: CHOOSE study.
summary: Main objective: The primary objective of the CHOOSE Study is to evaluate the efficacy of dostarlimab in young patients  newly diagnosed with dMMR EC who desire to preserve fertility
conditions: Newly diagnosed endometrial carcinomas of the MMR-deficient molecular subtype
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1.	Voluntary written informed consent of the participant or their legally authorized representative has been obtained prior to any screening procedures 2.	Use of highly effective methods of birth control; defined as those that, alone or in combination, result in a low failure rate (i.e., less than 1% per year) when used consistently and correctly; such as implants, injectables, combined oral contraceptives. Sexual abstinence is considered a highly effective method only if defined as refraining from heterosexual intercourse during the entire period of risk associated with the study intervention. The reliability of sexual abstinence will be evaluated in relation to the duration of the clinical study and the preferred and usual lifestyle of the participant. Contraception must be maintained starting with the screening visit through 4 months (120 days) after the last dose of dostarlimab 3.	 Women older than 18 and younger than 45 years, with a strong desire to preserve their fertility 4.	Histological new diagnosis of endometrioid EC, grade G1 or G2, without lymphovascular space invasion 5.	Radiological diagnosis of 2009 FIGO stage IA (2023 FIGO stage IA1), without myometrium or cervical invasion obtained through pelvic MRI or pelvic ultrasound performed by an expert sonographer 6.	MMR deficiency as assessed by immunohistochemistry or MSI-H as assessed by polymerase chain reaction or next-generation sequencing performed in a certified laboratory. MMR deficiency or MSI-H need to be tested on an adequate tumor sample. The presence of germline dMMR/MSH-I doesn’t represent an exclusion criterion 7.	A negative serum pregnancy test at enrollment, within 72 hours of the first dose of dostarlimab, and for each other dose 8.	Adequate organ function, defined as: o   Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 1,500/µL o   Platelets ≥ 100,000/µL c o   Hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL or ≥ 5.6 mmol/L d o   Serum creatinine ≤ 1.5× upper limit of normal (ULN) or calculated creatinine clearance ≥ 50 mL/min using Cockcroft-Gault equation for patients with creatinine levels > 1.5× institutional ULN o   Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5× ULN AND direct bilirubin ≤ 1× ULN. Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ≤ 2.5× ULN •	International normalized ratio (INR) or prothrombin time (PT) ≤1.5× ULN unless the patient is receiving anticoagulant therapy as long as PT or partial thromboplastin (PTT) is within the therapeutic range of intended use of anticoagulants. Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) ≤1.5× ULN unless the patient is receiving anticoagulant therapy as long as PT or PTT is within the therapeutic range of intended use of anticoagulants.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1.	Participant has a history of prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-1-ligand-1 (anti-PD-L1), or anti-PD-1 ligand-2 (anti-PD-L2) agent 2.	Subject has received prior hormonal FST for endometrial cancer  3.	Patient has evidence of extra-uterine disease 4.	Any disorder, which in the Investigator’s opinion might jeopardise the participant’s safety or compliance with the protocol 5.	Any prior or concomitant treatment(s) that might jeopardise the participant’s safety or that would compromise the integrity of the Trial  6.	A known additional malignancy that progressed or required active treatment within the last 2 years. Exceptions include basal cell carcinoma of the skin, squamous cell carcinoma of the skin that has undergone potentially curative therapy, or in situ cervical cancer 7.	Serious, uncontrolled medical disorder, non-malignant systemic diseases, or active infection requiring systemic therapy 8.	Pregnant patients 9.	Breastfeeding patient who is not willing to stop breastfeeding during the treatment 10.	Patient is expecting/plans to conceive children within the projected duration of the study, starting with the screening visit through 120 days after the last dose of study treatment 11.	Patients with a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or receive systemic steroid therapy or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior to the first dose of study treatment 12.	Patient has a known history of the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) (HIV 1/2 antibodies), known active hepatitis B (e.g., hepatitis B surface antigen [HBsAg] reactive) or hepatitis C (e.g., hepatitis C virus ribonucleic acid [HCV RNA] [qualitative] is detected) 13.	Patient has an active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in the past 2 years (i.e., with the use of disease-modifying agents, corticosteroids, or immunosuppressive drugs). Replacement therapy is not considered a form of systemic therapy (e.g., thyroid hormone or insulin) 14.	Patient has a history of interstitial lung disease 15.	Patient has participated in another study of an investigational agent and received study therapy or used an investigational device within 4 weeks prior to the first dose of the study drug 16.	Patient has not recovered adequately (≤ Grade 1) from AEs and/or complications from any major surgery prior to starting therapy 17.	Patient has received a live vaccine within 30 days of the planned start of study therapy 18.	Patient has a known hypersensitivity to dostarlimab components or excipients 19.	Patient has experienced any of the following with prior immunotherapy: Any immune-mediated AE of grade 3 or higher, immune-related severe neurologic events of any grade (e.g. myasthenic syndrome/myasthenia gravis, encephalitis, Guillain Barré Syndrome, or transverse myelitis), exfoliative dermatitis of any grade (Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, or drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms [DRESS] syndrome), or myocarditis of any grade. Non-clinically significant laboratory abnormalities are not exclusionary 20.	Patient has clinically significant cardiovascular disease within 6 months of enrollment 21.	Patient has cirrhosis or unstable liver or biliary disease per investigator assessment defined by the presence of ascites, encephalopathy, coagulopathy, hypoalbuminemia, esophageal/gastric varices, or persistent jaundice. NOTE: Stable non-cirrhotic chronic liver disease (including Gilbert’s syndrome or asymptomatic gallstones) is acceptable if participant otherwise meets entry criteria
